neighborhoods.name: Garapan
neighborhoods.description: Saipan's main tourist and commercial district on the west coast, home to Micro Beach, the American Memorial Park, hotels, restaurants, and the island's largest concentration of shops and services
neighborhoods.character: Tourist hub, beachfront, commercial, walkable core, nightlife

housing.predominantType: Newer condo buildings and hotel-adjacent apartments, at a premium over the island's mostly older rental stock

neighborhoods.character_notes: Garapan is the most convenient base for a retiree without daily driving: the Commonwealth Healthcare Corporation hospital (the CNMI's only hospital) sits on Navy Hill Road at the edge of the district, and pharmacies, banks, and groceries are minutes away. Under Article 12 of the CNMI Constitution only persons of Northern Marianas descent can own land, so non-NMD retirees rent or take long-term leases capped at 55 years — there is no conventional home purchase, which is why no buy price is listed. Serious medical care beyond CHCC's capabilities means medevac to Guam, the Philippines, or Hawaii, and the island carries real typhoon exposure (Super Typhoon Yutu in 2018 was among the strongest storms ever to hit US soil).

sources.title: Numbeo - Cost of Living in Saipan

neighborhoods.name: Susupe
neighborhoods.description: The civic center of Saipan just south of Garapan, holding the CNMI courts, government offices, Kilili Beach Park, and the Sugar Dock, with a lagoon-front residential fringe
neighborhoods.character: Civic center, government offices, lagoon beaches, quiet, mid-island convenience

housing.predominantType: Older concrete apartment blocks and single-family homes

neighborhoods.character_notes: Susupe offers flat terrain, beach access at Kilili and Sugar Dock, and a 10-minute drive to the CHCC hospital in Garapan — practical for retirees who want calm without isolation. There is no public bus system on Saipan, so a car is essential for groceries, medical visits, and errands; taxis exist but are expensive for daily use. Rental stock is mostly older concrete construction, which is typhoon-resistant but dated.

neighborhoods.name: Chalan Kanoa
neighborhoods.description: A historic southwestern village that was Saipan's largest settlement after World War II, centered on Mount Carmel Cathedral, with a beachside grid of streets and local shops
neighborhoods.character: Historic, local village life, cathedral, beachside grid, affordable

housing.predominantType: Older single-family homes and small apartment buildings

neighborhoods.character_notes: Chalan Kanoa is flat, gridded, and lived-in, with churches, small stores, and the post office close together — good for retirees who want authentic village life at below-Garapan rents, about 15 minutes by car from the CHCC hospital. Southern Saipan took heavy damage from Super Typhoon Yutu in 2018, so favor concrete construction and check a unit's storm history and generator situation before signing a lease. A car is essential; there is no public transit.

neighborhoods.name: San Vicente
neighborhoods.description: An elevated residential village on Saipan's eastern side near Magicienne Bay, south of Mount Tapochau, favored by long-term residents for its cooler breezes and views
neighborhoods.character: Residential, elevated, breezy, family neighborhoods, quiet

housing.predominantType: Single-family concrete homes, some with ocean views

neighborhoods.character_notes: San Vicente trades convenience for elevation, quiet, and some of the island's better residential views over Magicienne Bay; rents sit toward the affordable end of Saipan's $750-1,600 range. It is entirely car-dependent — expect 15-20 minutes of driving to the CHCC hospital and Garapan shopping — so it suits retirees who are comfortable behind the wheel. Because Article 12 bars non-NMD land ownership, even long-stay retirees here are renters or 55-year leaseholders, never owners.
